title: Repository Maintenance
description: Keep your Git repository fast and healthy with regular maintenance commands.

data.text: Over time, Git repositories accumulate loose objects, unreachable commits, stale refs, and bloated pack files. Regular maintenance keeps the repository fast and prevents disk usage from growing without bound.

items: **git gc**: Packs loose objects, removes unreachable objects, and prunes reflogs
**git prune**: Removes unreachable objects (older than prune.time)
**git repack**: Repacks pack files into fewer, larger packs
**git fsck**: Verifies the integrity of the repository
**git prune-packed**: Removes loose objects that are already in pack files

data.title: Run full repository maintenance
data.code:
# Run garbage collection (packs objects and prunes)
git gc --aggressive --prune=now

# Verify repository integrity
git fsck --full

# Repack pack files into a single pack
git repack -a -d --depth=250 --window=250

# Prune packed objects (remove duplicates)
git prune-packed

# Check repository size
du -sh .git

data.text: git gc is the primary maintenance command. It runs automatically when loose objects exceed the gc.auto threshold (default: 6700 objects). Use --aggressive for deeper optimization, but be aware that it is slower.

data.title: Configure git gc behavior
data.code:
# See current gc configuration
git config --list | grep gc

# Key settings:
# gc.auto = 6700 (auto-run when loose objects exceed this)
# gc.autoPackLimit = 50 (repack when pack files exceed this)
# gc.pruneExpire = 2.weeks.ago (prune objects older than this)

# Configure aggressive gc schedule
git config gc.auto 10000
git config gc.autoPackLimit 100

# Run gc manually with custom prune time
git gc --prune="1.week.ago"

data.text: git fsck checks the repository for corruption, dangling objects, and missing references. Run it after maintenance or when you suspect disk corruption.

data.title: Verify repository integrity
data.code:
# Full integrity check
git fsck --full

# Output shows:
# - dangling commit (orphaned commit not reachable from any ref)
# - dangling blob (orphaned file content)
# - dangling tree (orphaned directory tree)
# - missing blob (corrupted object)

# Dangling objects are normal after branch deletion
# or rebase. They are cleaned up by git gc.

# Check only for errors (no dangling output)
git fsck --no-reflogs

data.text: Bare repositories (central Git servers) accumulate objects from every push. Run git gc regularly on bare repositories to keep them fast. Use git gc --auto in a cron job.

data.title: Automate gc for bare repositories
data.code:
# Add to crontab (run weekly)
# 0 2 * * 0 cd /opt/git/project.git && git gc --auto

# Or use a systemd timer
# /etc/systemd/system/git-gc.service
[Unit]
Description=Git garbage collection

[Service]
Type=oneshot
WorkingDirectory=/opt/git/project.git
ExecStart=/usr/bin/git gc --auto

# /etc/systemd/system/git-gc.timer
[Unit]
Description=Weekly git gc

[Timer]
OnCalendar=weekly

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target

data.title: Never run --prune=now on shared repositories
data.text: git gc --prune=now immediately deletes all unreachable objects. On a shared repository, another user may still have a branch pointing to an object you consider unreachable. Use the default prune time (2 weeks) on shared repos.
Over time, pack files accumulate delta chains that become inefficient. Use git repack to create new, optimized pack files and delete the old ones.

data.title: Repack and optimize pack files
data.code:
# Repack all objects into a single pack file
git repack -a -d --depth=250 --window=250

# -a: repack all objects
# -d: delete redundant pack files after repack
# --depth=250: maximum delta chain depth
# --window=250: window size for delta compression

# Verify the result
git count-objects -vH

items.question: Can git gc cause data loss?
items.answer: No. git gc only removes unreachable objects (objects not referenced by any ref, reflog, or index). Reachable objects are always preserved.

items.question: How do I recover a dangling commit?
items.answer: Use git fsck --full to list dangling commits. Use git log <commit-sha> or git show <commit-sha> to inspect them. Use git branch <name> <sha> to recover a dangling commit.

items.question: Does git gc affect performance while it runs?
items.answer: Yes. git gc is CPU and I/O intensive. Run it during low-traffic periods for shared repositories. For local repos, it is usually fast enough to run interactively.

items.question: What is the difference between git gc and git prune?
items.answer: git gc runs prune as one of its steps. git gc also packs objects, prunes reflogs, and optimizes the repository. git prune only removes unreachable objects and does not pack.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: git gc is the primary maintenance command; run it regularly
git gc --prune=now aggressively deletes unreachable objects
Use git repack to shrink pack files and improve delta compression
Verify integrity with git fsck --full after maintenance
